title: fix(console): Home answers a navigation can() gate from the one /auth/me/permissions source (objectui#12700)
body:
Fixes #12700
Clause-②: no

Part 2 of objectui#12700 (part 1 landed as `71243db`). Measured: no published export changes shape. `DefaultHomeLayout`'s props are unchanged, and the new `ConsolePermissionsScope` lives in the console app, not in a published package's entry.

## What changed

- **One permission source over `/home` and `/apps/:appName/*`** (`apps/console`). The `MePermissionsProvider` that `AppContent` mounted for `/apps` alone is now `ConsolePermissionsScope` in `AppContent.tsx`. It has the same endpoint, the same authenticated fetcher, and the same loading and error-with-Retry fallbacks. `App.tsx` mounts it once, as the element of a pathless layout route (ProtectedRoute, then the scope, then the router Outlet) whose only children are `/home` and `/apps/:appName/*`. Moving between the two keeps the layout element, so the instance survives and there is one `/auth/me/permissions` request per session load. There is no second fetch, cache or provider instance. `AppContent` keeps `LocalizationFetchProvider`, `ApprovalRecordReads` and `WorkspaceTimezonePrompt`, which still render under the scope.
- **Home's navigation predicate scope binds the map** (`packages/app-shell/src/console/home/HomeLayout.tsx`). `HomeLayout` mounts an `ExpressionProvider`, which reads `useExpressionPermissions`. So the gates evaluated on Home answer `current_user.can(OBJECT, VERB)` from the payload: the bell's and the activity card's roster (`useNavMemberGates` through `activityObjectRoster`), and the command palette's navigation list. Only the permissions are bound. The other scope inputs are stable module constants: no identity and no features, exactly the scope the no-provider default gave Home before.
- **`/studio/*` is untouched.** Its routes, `studioEntry.ts` and the builder subtree are not edited, and they sit beside the layout route, outside the context.

## Premise, verified before any code

I checked the premise first: does anything `/home` renders change its output for a permission holder once a `PermCtx` is above it? The Home route element's module graph was walked from `HomeLayout` and `HomePage`, 129 modules. Every module that reads the permission context was enumerated. For each one rendered on Home, here is what it does without and with the context:

| Consumer on Home | Reads | No context | With context, holder | With context, non-holder |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bell and Home activity feed (`useSharedActivityFeed`) | `isLoaded`, `can(sys_activity, read)` | unknown, so reads | grant, so reads (same) | refused, so no widget (as on /apps) |
| Home inbox (`useHomeInbox`) | `isLoaded`, `can(INBOX_OBJECT, read)` | reads | reads (same) | refused (as on /apps) |
| Activity roster (`useNavMemberGates`) | `can`, `hasCapabilities`, evaluator | all true; a can() gate faults and is withheld (part 1) | true (same); **a can() gate now answers and the entry is included** | entry dropped as a verdict, no report |
| Command palette record search (`useRecordSearch` fieldReadPolicy) | `isLoaded`, `checkField` | not loaded, so labelled as served | readable field, so the same label | denied field stripped from the label (as on /apps) |
| Command palette nav list | evaluator | as the roster | as the roster | as the roster |
| `HomePage` authoring gate (`useCanAuthorMetadata`) | `hasCapabilities` | unknown, so open | held, so open (same) | refused (as on /apps) |

So the only change for a holder is the intended one: a granted `can()` gate now includes its entry. The other context-dependent modules in the graph are not rendered inside the Home route element. Two are rendered by `ConnectedShell`, above the route, where they are outside the context on both `/home` and `/apps`: `useConsoleActionRuntime` and its dialogs. Two are only imported: `deriveRelatedLists` and `ConsoleShell`'s `resolveSetupAppPath`.

One reading for the seat: with the context, an object the payload does not mention answers "denied" for an authenticated session. Studio's note treats that as a holder change, because the builder renders objects outside the payload. On Home, every object reached is a published object from the apps' navigation, judged by the same payload the same components already read on `/apps`. So it is a non-holder verdict, not a holder change.

## A1, measured

`/home` and `/apps/:appName/*` were sibling top-level routes, each with its own ProtectedRoute, so they had no common ancestor below ProtectedRoute. A pathless layout route makes one, and Studio stays where it is. That is the shape used here.

## Pins (`apps/console/src/__tests__/App.homePermissions-12700.test.tsx`)

Real parts: `App`'s route tree, `ConsolePermissionsScope` and `MePermissionsProvider`, `HomeLayout` and its `ExpressionProvider`, `useNavMemberGates`, `activityObjectRoster`, the formula engine, and Studio's entry gate. Mocked: the network, i.e. the console's authenticated fetcher. ProtectedRoute is reduced to the metadata context its `ConnectedShell` provides.

- (a) A fresh `/home` with a denied payload: the gated entry is absent from the roster, and no `app-shell:visible` line is logged.
- (b) Granted: present, and no line is logged.
- (c) `/home` then `/apps/crm`: one `/auth/me/permissions` request in total. Also: Home shows the loading screen until the answer arrives.
- (d) CONTROL: the Studio builder renders with no `PermCtx` above it.
- (e) CONTROL: part 1's pins stay green (`UnifiedSidebar.navCanPermissions-12700`, `navigationVisibility-12700`, `currentUserCan-4421.render`, `AppContent.landingMemberGates-12426`).

**Ablation 1: the mount move.** The fix was committed first. `App.tsx` was then mutated so `/home` sits on its own ProtectedRoute without the scope; on disk, mutant marker 1 and fix marker 0. Result: 3 failed, 2 passed. (a) failed on the warning (`expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`), (b) failed (`expected 'crm_account' to be 'crm_account,crm_forecast'`), and the loading pin failed. The file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, its blob equals HEAD's (`428947b95`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**Ablation 2: Home's ExpressionProvider removed, mount kept.** Result: 2 failed. (a) failed on the warning and (b) on the roster. Restored, and the blob equals HEAD's (`030429618`).

Neither ablation involves a dist or build leg: the console project resolves `@object-ui/*` to `src` through its alias.

## Verification (HEAD `c7eb44573`)

- **Closure builds.** `turbo build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`: 28/28. `--filter='@object-ui/console^...'`: 34/34.
- **type-check.** `@object-ui/app-shell` (tsc and tsconfig.test.json) exit 0. `@object-ui/console` exit 0, which includes the test files. The first console run showed one error of mine: an unused React import in the new test, now fixed. Its other errors were unbuilt dependency dists, which the closure build resolved.
- **vitest, `--maxWorkers=1`.**
  - Final run on `c7eb44573`: the new pin, part 1's sidebar and visibility pins, and the HomeLayout palette test: 4 files, 21 passed.
  - On `4aa5c2be7` (the later commit only removed an import): every console test that reads `App`, `AppContent`, `ProtectedRoute` or Studio routing, 28 files, 225 passed. Also part 1's pins plus `app-shell/src/console/home/` plus the two `AppHeader` home tests: 33 files, 255 passed.
- **Four existing tests mock `../AppContent`** (`App.docsPortalLazy`, `App.agentChatLink-10640`, `internalFormShell`, `i18nAfterSignIn-12034`). Their mocks now also export a pass-through `ConsolePermissionsScope`. Vitest throws on a missing mock export, and `App` reads the name on every render: measured red on `i18nAfterSignIn-12034` before the fix.
- **NOT MEASURED: the whole `apps/console` dir, and the whole app-shell package.** The console dir is 210 files, and one third of it is 617 s by the shard sequencer's timings, which is over the container's foreground cap. Narrowing declared: the 28-file set above is every console test that imports or mocks the changed composition. CI runs the full set.
- **eslint `--no-inline-config --format json` on the 8 changed ts/tsx files.** Population: `git diff --name-only` against the base. File count from the JSON: 8. Result: 0 errors, 1 warning (`react-refresh/only-export-components` on `systemRoutes`, present on the base at the same line). `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting, so untouched files' verdicts cannot move.
- **Gates, all exit 0:** check:phantom-deps, self-import, unreferenced-sources, doc-example-readers, handler-key-reads, side-effects-array, element-data-source-declaration, spec-symbols, action-forward-parity, designer-field-key-parity, icon-record-names, i18n-keys, i18n-drift, i18n-designer-parity, control-bytes, new-line-citations, test-path-roots, `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`. `check:spec-floors` was not run.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:eager-closure`** (needs a console vite build). By reading: the walk above found `ExpressionProvider` already reached from `HomeLayout` on the base, through `useNavMemberGates`. `MePermissionsProvider` was already eager through `AppContent`. So no module enters the eager closure.
- **NOT MEASURED: the card's screenshot acceptance** (HotCRM as a user without `crm_opportunity` read, 1280 px). No HotCRM backend is available in this container.

## Acceptance notes

- `apps/console/src/components/studioEntry.ts` still says the `/studio/*` routes sit outside "the only mount" of `PermCtx`, "`AppContent`, which covers `/apps/:appName/*`". The substance holds: Studio is still outside. But the mount is now the layout route over `/home` and `/apps`. The file is outside this card's surface, so it is left as is. Carrier: none.
- Home's predicate scope binds no `current_user` identity (unchanged from before this PR). A navigation gate naming `current_user.id` or `current_user.positions` still faults on Home and is withheld and reported once, while the in-app sidebar answers it. No producer serving such a gate was measured. Carrier: none.
- `DefaultHomeLayout` now mounts its own `ExpressionProvider`. A host that wrapped it in an `ExpressionProvider` of its own would have that scope shadowed under Home. No such host is known in this tree.
- Loading posture: Home now waits on `/auth/me/permissions` behind the same loading screen and Retry error screen `/apps` uses. Pinned in (c).
